name: What should be included in an ADU bathroom contractor estimate?

mainEntity.name: What line items should homeowners check before accepting a quote for an ADU bathroom project?
mainEntity.text: What line items should homeowners check before accepting a quote for an ADU bathroom project?

acceptedAnswer.text: A strong ADU bathroom estimate should be detailed enough to show what is actually included and what could become a change order later. At minimum, homeowners should look for demolition, framing, rough plumbing, rough electrical, waterproofing, tile or wall finishes, fixture allowances, ventilation, permits, inspections, and final cleanup. If the project involves a slab cut, sewer tie-in, or trenching, those items should be called out separately. It also helps if the bid specifies who is supplying the toilet, vanity, shower valve, lighting, and glass enclosure, since allowances can vary widely. In Los Angeles-area projects, a vague lump-sum quote can hide expensive surprises once the bathroom layout is finalized. A good estimate should explain how the bathroom connects to the sewer, whether venting is included, and what happens if concealed conditions are found. Comparing detailed bids is much easier than comparing one-line totals, and it reduces the chance of budget overruns after work starts.
acceptedAnswer.description: A useful ADU bathroom estimate should break out demolition, framing, plumbing, electrical, waterproofing, tile, fixtures, ventilation, permits, and cleanup. It should also say whether inspections, disposal, and change orders are included. Vague lump-sum bids are harder to compare and more likely to hide extra costs.
